candidate.answerReason: Meshed gears pass equal numbers of teeth through each contact per minute. Consequently, tooth count times rotational speed is the same for all three gears, giving reciprocal speed ratios.

methods.label: Count teeth passing each contact
methods.explanation:
At a contact between two meshed gears, each passing tooth on one gear must be matched by a tooth on the other. Therefore, the two gears pass the same number of teeth through their contact each minute.

Let \(a,b,c\) be the speeds of gears \(A,B,C\), respectively, in revolutions per minute. One revolution of \(A\) passes \(x\) teeth, so its tooth-passage rate is \(xa\). Applying the same reasoning at the two contacts shown gives
\[
xa=yb=zc.
\]
Thus speed is inversely proportional to the number of teeth:
\[
a:b:c=\frac1x:\frac1y:\frac1z.
\]
The tooth counts \(x,y,z\) are positive, so multiplying every term of this ratio by \(xyz\) gives
\[
a:b:c=yz:xz:xy.
\]
Adjacent gears turn in opposite directions, but speed measures the number of revolutions per minute without a direction sign. The required proportion is \(\boxed{yz:xz:xy}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Counting teeth per revolution establishes a constant product, requiring only elementary inverse proportion and ratios.

candidate.annotationRationale: The mathematical target is recognizing inverse proportion from the constant tooth-passage rate. The method uses ratios, reciprocals of positive tooth counts, and division of equal products. Direct proportion and circle formulas are not required by this route. These annotations do not establish student mastery.

review.mathematicalCheck: The figure shows contacts between A and B and between B and C. Equal tooth-passage rates give xa=yb=zc, hence a:b:c=1/x:1/y:1/z=yz:xz:xy. Positive tooth counts justify the reciprocals and common multiplier. The distinction between speed and signed rotation correctly handles opposite turning directions.
review.levelCheck: Counting teeth per revolution supplies an accessible explanation of inverse proportion, with no unnecessary advanced machinery.
review.methodDistinctness: The single tooth-counting method is complete and sufficient.
review.annotationCheck: Inverse proportion is the appropriate assessed target. Ratios, reciprocals, and equality transformations are justified shared supports and method prerequisites; no circle formula or direct-proportion prerequisite is imposed.
